selections.selectionRationale: The inverse-coupled gauges make the claim physical: every tick of approval that fills the top bar visibly drains the energy bar beneath it, so 'pleasing everyone is exhausting' is read as a mechanism, not a slogan. Opposite-direction ProgressBars are legible muted, use only registered primitives, and keep one dominant gold accent on the headline.

The card's trajectory reversing mid-arc physically enacts 'post, then delete' as one motion event, so the forward slide being cancelled by a returning pull and glow decay makes self-censorship legible without narration. It is a single-object beat with the strongest cold-viewer decode, distinct from prior memory entries in metaphor and composition.

Contradiction proof makes the futility logical: identical input stamped BAIK and SOMBONG at the same instant proves no action can satisfy the approval function. The split layout enacts the script's opposites pattern so a cold viewer reads the judgment as being about itself, not the subject.

One red stroke starting before the first checkpoint and running past the last without lifting enacts the semanticMechanism: judgment is the track itself, not a reaction, so a single unbroken mark over all four states performs 'no behavior escapes verdict' without narration.

The slack-string state makes the beat's 'buat apa?' answer itself by physical subtraction: the pulling source is visibly gone, so the standing figure proves agency without narration. It enacts the question as a state change rather than naming it, using only registered primitives (Line/Circle/Stack/WordReveal) with a single gold accent on 'APA'.

The dial's semanticMechanism — input noise stays constant on one side while the pointer's rotation visibly attenuates only what reaches 'your life' — physically performs 'seberapa besar pengaruh' as a magnitude a viewer has hand-tuned before, so control is felt as attenuation rather than asserted.

One ring's glow fades fully out while the other holds and intensifies, enacting the separation of stakes instead of naming it. Two circles, one glow: instantly legible to a cold viewer and consistent with dualObject.

The seal's semanticMechanism — a stamp presses down once, hardens, and its unbroken ring closes to external editing — physically enacts the closing verdict 'not made for everyone' as finality rather than consolation. A cold viewer reads the landing stamp as 'decided, official' without narration, so the phrase becomes the inscription on an irreversible identity mark.
